Command: An impure priest after immersion shall not serve until sundown
Summary: The command: An impure priest after immersion shall not serve until sundown (Leviticus 22:7). A priest who washed for uncleanness remained unclean until evening, and only then might eat of the holy things.
Commandment: An impure priest after immersion shall not serve until sundown.
Application: This row narrows the parent group command to this one mitzvah. The moral/ceremonial/civil division is a traditional classification, not Scripture's own division; this law is traditionally classed as ceremonial. The New Testament replaces the whole system of holy food: all who are in Christ are a holy priesthood (1 Peter 2:5,9), and the meal that marks God's people is the Lord's Supper, not the priestly portions. The boundary itself — holy things are not common things — is fulfilled, not continued.
Purpose: Scripture's stated ground: the holy things are the LORD's, set apart for the priesthood (Leviticus 22:3-16).
Function: A priest who washed for uncleanness remained unclean until evening, and only then might eat of the holy things — a ceremonial law of waiting for the sunset. Its goal was to keep the boundary of the day: the washing began the cleansing, but the evening completed it. The evil was rushing back to holy things before the cleansing was finished, treating the washing as instant. It restrained that by the sundown: the priest waited, and the evening said when he was clean again.
